title: Direct Positioning
content: ### Objective Activate Direct Positioning to click to easily arrange Patterns and OBJs. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Click 3D Pattern or OBJ ▶ ![Direct_Positioning.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438211305497) Direct Positioning ### Operation 1. Follow the path: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Click 3D Pattern or OBJ ▶ ![Direct_Positioning.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438211305497) Direct Positioning 2. Hover the mouse over a Garment or Avatar. → The selected Pattern or OBJ moves along with the mouse cursor. 3. Click to place the Pattern in the desired location. ※Note: When arranging Patterns, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to restrict Pattern rotation (ver4.0.0).
content_description: Learn how to easily arrange 3D Patterns and OBJs using the Direct Positioning feature in the 3D Toolbar.

title: Show/Hide Sewing
content: ### Objective When Sewing Lines are too complicated, hide them for clear view as needed. ### Location 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Show Sewing (All) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Show Sewing (All) → The selected Sewing Lines or all Sewing Lines show or disappear from the 2D and the 3D window.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to hide or show sewing lines in 2D and 3D views for improved clarity during complex sewing tasks.

title: Change Length
content: ### Objective Type in the segment length and edit Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the segment to be adjusted to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Change Length. → The Change Length window appears. 3. Enter the length of the segment and select the desired location. → The preview shows in the 2D window. 4. Click OK. → The segment length is changed accordingly. ※Note: If a line connected to the selected line is a curve, the curve point is moved according to the changed length. If the "Lock Curve Points" option is checked, only straight points can be moved. (ver MD10)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for editing segment lengths in 2D patterns using the editing tools in the software.

title: Edit Topstitch
content: ### Objective Relocate or adjust length of Topstitches. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch ### Operation #### Relocate Topstitch 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch 2. Click on a topstitch to change its location. → The selected Topstitch is being highlighted. 3. Drag to a desired location. #### Adjust Topstitch Length 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch 2. Click and drag one of the two end points of a Topstitch to adjust its length. → The selected Topstitch is now being adjusted.
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for relocating or adjusting the length of topstitches within the design interface.

title: Fold Seam Line
content: ### Objective Use this function to create an pressing effect on sewn parts of Patterns. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Fold Angle ### Operation 1. Click on Edit Sewing tool. 2. Select the seamline to change its fold angle. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Fold Angle 4. Adjust the value, in the range of 0~360˚. ※ Note: * The value of fold angle is in between 0° to 360°, 180° represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0˚, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360˚. * #### Fold Strength The intensity of the fold is able to be set by adjusting the value of Fold Strength. The higher the value, the closer the fold is to the set angle. When a jacket and its lining are sewn together, the sewn area inflates due to the default sewing angle and intensity values. In this case, sets the Fold Strength to 0 to flatten the sewn boundaries. * When the Sewing type is set as Turned, Fold Strength and Fold Angle cannot be modified (ver4.0.0).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the fold angle and strength of sewn parts in Patterns to achieve desired pressing effects.

title: Edit Curve Point
content: ### ### ### ### ### ### Objective Add and edit curve points on Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Curve Point ### Operation **Add** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Click the desired position of a segment to add a curve point. Or, Right click on a segment to split the segment by a curve point (ver 7.1) **Split into Two Lines** | Adjust by entering the length of both lines which are divided by the right clicked point, or by entering the ratio. ---|--- **Split by Length** | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. You can change the direction in which a point is added to a start/opposite/center basis. **Uniform Split** | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. → A free curve point is created at the selected point. → When a free curve point is added to an Bezier curve, the curvarture is changed based on the free curve point. **Move** 1. Click and drag a curve point or press the arrow key on the keyboard to move. To enter Moved Distance, right click while click-and-dragging the Curve Point **Distance Moved** | Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. ---|--- **X/ Y Axis** | Type in how much a point is moved on X/ Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments. ※ Note: * Moving multiple curve points at once is possible starting ver4.2.0 (ver4.2.0). The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers; by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) * The Free Curve Point can be freely added and edited. The Free Curve Point can also be created by holding down the Ctrl key on the keyboard while drafting a Pattern with the Polygon tool. * When a Free Curve Point is added to an AI Bezier curve, its AI Bezier curve handles disappear and the curve is reshaped based on the added Free Curve Point.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for adding and editing curve points on pattern outlines and internal lines to enhance 2D pattern design.

title: Match 2D Pattern Measurements
content: ### Objective Match up the pattern line lengths of two corresponding pattern outlines or segment points (ver3.0.0). ### Location #### Match Up with Pattern Outlines Right-Click the Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) ▶ Match Up ▶ To Start/ To Center/ To End #### Match Up with Points Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Point) ▶ Match Up ### Operation #### Match up with Pattern Outlines 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Edit Pattern Tool. 2. Select Pattern outlines of two separate Patterns that are intended to be aligned with each other. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) ▶ Match Up ▶ To Start / To Center / To End →The Patterns align to the Pattern outline that is right clicked on. #### Match Up with Points 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Edit Pattern Tool. 2. Select two points from the two Patterns that are intended to be aligned with each other. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Point) ▶ Match Up →The Patterns will align in reference to the point that is right clicked on first. #### Match Measurement (ver. 2024.0) 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Edit Pattern Tool. 2. Select Pattern outlines from the two separate Patterns that should be aligned adjacent to each other. Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) ▶ Match Up ▶ Match Measurement → Set the options as needed and then click the OK button. Match to | Choose the reference of the two segments. ---|--- Direction | Select the direction in which the segment will be edited. Measurement | The length of the segment to be matched is displayed. → The two line segments will be matched according to the setting options selected.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for aligning pattern outlines and segment points in design software, ensuring precise matching of lengths and positions.

title: Create Piping
content: ### Objective Create piping along with Garment seamlines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Piping ▶ Piping 3D Toolbar ▶ Piping ### ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. →Dash-lines appear along the edges of the Garment where piping is applicable. 2. On a 3D Garment or 2D Pattern (ver MD10), click the desired starting point, drag to extend, then double click to complete the Piping. → The Piping is now being created as designed. ※ Note: To create Piping on the entire circumference of a single Pattern, click on the first point of the Pattern outline ▶ click on the second point ▶ click back on the first point.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating piping along garment seamlines using the Piping 3D Toolbar.

title: Select/Move (3D)
content: ### Objective Select and move Patterns in the 3D window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move 2. Click and drag a part of the 3D Garment while the Simulate tool is activated. → The 3D Garment moves naturally, and you may fine-tune your 3D Garment. 3. Or, click and drag a part of the 3D Garment while the Simulate tool is deactivated. → Convert the 3D window to pattern arrangement mode and move the Garment as Patterns.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for selecting and moving patterns within the 3D window of the garment design software.

title: Binding (ver. 11)
content: ## Create Binding ### Objective Easily create Binding along Pattern Outlines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Binding ▶ Binding 3D Toolbar ▶ Binding ### Operation 1\. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Binding can be created appear in dashed lines. 2\. On a 3D Garment or 2D Pattern, click the start point and double click where you want to finish the Binding. → Binding is created on the selected segment. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. ## Select Binding ### Objective Edit Binding Properties. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Binding ▶ Select Binding 3D Toolbar ▶ Select Binding ※Note: 3D toolbar ▶ Select bindings with the Select/Move tool. ### Operation 1\. Select the tool/menu indicated. → The line segment for which the binding was created is displayed. 2\. Select the Binding to be edited. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 3\. Configure each property as needed referring to below table. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- Name | Rename Binding's name. Line Length | Check Binding's length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. Type | Under | Bindings are placed under the Patterns to express Inside Bindings. Over | Bindings are placed over the Patterns. Both | Bindings are placed both direction of the Patterns. Dimension | Width | Adjust selected Binding's width. (1~50mm) Length | Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50% ~ 200%) or a specific value. Particle Distance | Edit selected Binding's Particle Distance (4~20mm) Add'l Thickness - Collision | Adjust Binding's Add'l Thickness - Collision. Fabric | Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. Grain Direction | Bias/ Warp/ Custom | Choose among Bias, Warp, or Custom for the Binding's grain direction. Angle | Manually insert Angle value to set the Binding's grain direction. Topstitch | Add Topstitch to the Binding. The Topstitch option shows the styles which are added in the Topstitch tab of Object Browser. Sewing Line Type | Edit Binding's Sewing Line Type. Extend | Set whether to extend the binding after creating it on a part of the line segment. ※ Note: Binding Extension is not possible in the following cases. When the angle of both segments are more than 180 degrees based on the binding start/end point. 4\. Right-click on the Binding to be edited. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- Delete | Delete selected Binding. Reset Arrangement | Reset Binding's position. Use this option to fix unstable simulations. Deactivate / Activate | Deactivate or activate selected Binding. Freeze / Unfreeze | Freeze or unfreeze selected Binding. Flip Normal | The selected Binding's face flips to the other side.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide comprehensive guidance on creating and editing Binding along Pattern Outlines within a 3D garment design software.

title: Mac - Certificate Authentication Issues After Installation
content: ### Objective How to solve certificate authentication issues after installation in Mac. ### Operation #### OPTION 1 ※Note: Please make sure to [download](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358396498969) both certificate files from the links below to allow the program to run properly. 1. Click on the link to download the Certificate_1(certificate.crt) /Certificate_2(IntermediateCA.crt) file. 2. Navigate to the folder where the Certificate file was downloaded. 3. Double-click the Certificate file, then click Add. 4. Keychain Access window appears. 5. Double-click on the Certificate file in the Keychain Access window. 6. The certificate information appears, then click on Trust to expand its menu. 7. Under "When using this certificate" set it to Always Trust from the drop-down menu. 8. Restart the computer. 9. Start the program. #### OPTION 2 ※ Note: Should OPTION 1 fail to solve the issue, please use OPTION 2. 1. Click on the link to download the Certificate_1(certificate.crt) / Certificate_2(IntermediateCA.crt)/ Certificate_3(china-certificate.crt) file. 2. Run Terminal.app. ![Mac_Install_error_1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438736926745) 3. Enter "cd" then locate the folder where the file was downloaded in Finder, and drag and drop into Terminal.app. ![Mac_Install_error_2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438737153177) ※Note: Possible Errors Confirm if there is a space after cd. Confirm that the file path to where the downloaded file is located is correct. 4. Press Enter on the keyboard, input "ls-al" then press Enter on the keyboard again. ![Mac_Install_error_3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438737360153) ![Mac_Install_error_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438737620505) 5. Input sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k/Library/Keychains/System.keychain certificate.crt sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k/Library/Keychains/System.keychain IntermediateCA.crt sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k/Library/Keychains/System.keychain china-certificate.crt then press Enter on the keyboard. ![Mac_Install_error_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438737822233) ![Mac_Install_error_6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438738049817) 6. Enter the password associated with the Mac account, then start the program.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions to resolve certificate authentication issues on Mac after installation.

Object Browser ▶ Select a button item in the Buttonhole Tab. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Shapes ▶ Drop-down menu on the right hand side → Preset button shapes appear in the menu. 3. title: Copy Topstitch Style
content: ### Objective Copy and modify an existing Topstitch style in order to change its properties. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Copy ### Operation 1. Object Browser ▶ Select a Topstitch style to copy 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Copy → A new Topstitch style with the same properties of the selected Topstitch style is now being copied.

title: Edit Line (3D Pattern) Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
content: ### Objective Edit desired 3D Pen lines using the right-click pop-up menu. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶3D Pen (Garment) (ver3.0.0). / Edit Line (3D Pattern) (ver5.0.0) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ 3D Pen (Garment) (ver3.0.0). / Edit Line (3D Pattern) (ver5.0.0) 2. Right click on the desired 3D Pen line. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Refer to the below table and select an appropriate option. Option | Description ---|--- Delete | Delete the selected 3D Pen line. Add Point | Add a Segment Point to the selected 3D Pen line. Add Curve Point | Add a Curve Point to the selected 3D Pen line. Cut | Cut the Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. Cut & Sew | Cut and sew the Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. Symmetric | Cut | Cut the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. Cut & Sew | Cut and sew the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. Trace as Internal Shape | Trace the selected 3D Pen line as Internal Shapes on the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern. Convert to Internal Shape | Convert the selected 3D Pen line as Internal Shapes on the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for editing 3D Pen lines using the right-click pop-up menu within the 3D Toolbar for garment design.

title: Add Point/Split Line
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Add points and split a segment into multiple segments. Just simply click or enter values to add points on segments. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Add Point/Split Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Add Point/Split Line ### Operation #### Add Point with a Click 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Add Point/Split Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Add Point/Split Line 2. Hover the mouse over the segment where the point is to be added. Then, click once. #### Add Point with Entered Values 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Add Point/Split Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Add Point/Split Line 2. Hover the mouse over the segment where the point is to be added. Right click to access the Split Line window. Enter the desired values as below: Split Into Two Lines | Line 1 / Line 2 | The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. The shorter side is indicated as Line 1, and the longer side is indicated as Line 2. Enter the desired value in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. ---|---|--- Ratio | The ratio of the line to be split is 100%. The line can be divided into two lines based on the ratio. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. This function is often used split a line into two identical segments or to add a point at its 33.3%. Split by Length | Segment Length | Enter the segment length which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select Reverse Direction. Number of Segments | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. It is set as 2 by default (ver3.2.0). Direction | Reverse the direction that points are added (ver3.2.0). Uniform Split | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. ※ Note: Additional points can be added to multiple segments as they are detected as a single line. To use this function, select multiple segments where additional points should added to, right-click then select Split (ver3.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to efficiently add points and split segments into multiple segments within a 2D pattern design tool.

title: Buttonhole Right-Click Menus
content: ### Objective Change status of buttonholes as desired. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) 2. Right-click on the buttonhole to edit. → Buttonhole related pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu | Description ---|--- Reset 3D Position | Reset to location of pre-simulation. Copy | Copy the selected buttonhole. Paste | Paste the selected buttonhole. Mirror Paste (Position Only) | Mirror paste the position of the selected buttonhole. Delete | Delete the selected buttonhole. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern | Duplicate the selected buttonhole to its symmetric pattern. Activate/Deactivate | Activate or deactivate the selected buttonhole. Freeze/Unfreeze | Freeze or unfreeze the selected buttonhole. Set Number of Sewing Layers | Set the number of sewing layers for the selected buttonhole. After setting the Number of Sewing Layers, use the Select/Move Button tool to adjust buttonholes' locations on each Patterns. Flip | Move the selected buttonhole to the opposite side. Align | Align selected buttonholes based on the selected options. Distribute | Distribute selected buttonholes horizontally or vertically with same intervals.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on how to change the status and manage buttonholes in your design using the 3D Toolbar and Main Menu options.

title: Roll Up Selected Area
content: ### Objective Roll up the selected area horizontally or vertically. ### Location Selected Area Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Roll Up Horizontally / Roll Up Vertically ### Operation 1. Select a desired area to flip with the Select Mesh tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Selected Area Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Roll Up Horizontally / Roll Up Vertically 3. Activate the Simulate tool. → The selected area is now being flipped over horizontally or vertically.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for rolling up a selected area horizontally or vertically using the right-click pop-up menu in the Simulate tool.

title: Add Point or Curve Point to Line (Avatar)
content: ### Objective Use the right-click pop-up menu to add a point or curve point to modify Lines (Avatar). ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Line (Avatar) → When the Avatar is draped in a Garment, the Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the Line (Avatar) where a point or curve point should be added. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Choose Add Point or Add Curve Point as needed. → Add Point: a segment point is added to the selected line. → Add Curve Point: a curve point is added to the selected line. 4. Select and move the added point or curve point by using the Edit Line (Avatar) tool to edit Line (Avatar).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the right-click pop-up menu to add and modify points or curve points on lines in the Avatar editing feature of the 3D Garment tool.

title: ZIPPER: Register Custom OBJ as Slider & Puller
content: ### Objective Allows the user to create custom components for zippers that function dynamically in the 3D Window exactly as default provided zipper components. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ Register OBJ 3D Toolbar ▶ Zipper Tool ▶ Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ '+' ### Operation 1. Create mesh for Zipper Puller or Slider and export as an OBJ. → If creating a single OBJ file for both Slider & Puller, the node for the Slider must be named "Slider," and the node for the Puller must be named "Puller" before export. 2. Navigate to either of the locations listed above under "Location" and click on 'Register OBJ' or the '+' icon in the Property Editor. 3. Select the relevant Type (Slider, Puller, Slider & Puller, Stopper). 4. In the File section of the pop-up window, click on the four-square button to navigate to the location of the custom OBJ file and Double-Click to select it. 5. Adjust the position of the Puller or Slider in the preview window. 6. Click 'OK'. 7. Load a garment with a Zipper. 8. Click on the Zipper in the 3D Window. 9. In the Property Editor for the Zipper, observe that the Slider, Puller, or Stopper the user has registered is now available to be assigned to the zipper. → You can find the custom Zipper component in the dropdown menu to the right of Slider or Puller under the 'Shape' section.
content_description: This webpage guides users in creating and registering custom 3D zipper components that function seamlessly within the application's dynamic environment.

title: Edit Color Swatch
content: ### Objective Rename, reorder, and reset color swatches and color palettes. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color ### Operation #### Rename Color Swatch 1. Select a desired object; Avatar/Fabric/Button/Topstitch/Etc. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color → The color palette window appears. 3. On the bottom-left side of the palette window, click on a color swatch to be renamed. → 'Color Swatch Name' window appears. 4. Rename as desired then either click on somewhere else or press Enter on the keyboard. → The selected color swatch's name is now being adjusted. #### #### ※ Note: #### Added Method in ver4.2.0 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Materials ▶ Color → The Color window appears. 2. Under the Default_Palette, double click a color swatch to change its name. → The Color Swatch Name window appears. 3. Type in the desired name and click OK. → Selected swatch's name is changed. #### Added Method in ver3.2.0 1. Select an item (Avatar, Fabric, Button, Topstitch, etc.) to change its color. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Color/ Specular Color/ Emission Color 3. Click on the color swatch on the left. → Type in the desired name when the name field is activated. 4. Type in the desired name. → The selected color swatch's name is changed. #### Reorder Color Swatch 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color 2. Click and drag color swatches to reorder as desired. #### Reset Custom Palette 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color → The Color Palette window appears. 2. Click x on the Default_Palette button on the top of the Palette Library. → All default colors are now being deleted.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for renaming, reordering, and resetting color swatches and palettes within the Property Editor's Material section.

title: Reverse Sewing

Select the Sewing Lines to be reversed. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ Reverse Sewing (Ctrl + B) → The Sewing Lines' Directional Notches are reversed.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for reversing the directional notches of sewing lines using the 2D/3D toolbar and right-click pop-up menu.

title: Add Perpendicular Internal Line
content: ### Objective Create Internal Lines perpendicular to Pattern outlines or 2D window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Add from a Point 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the point of a Pattern outline or Internal Line. →The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Hover the mouse over the Add Perpendicular Internal Line option. → Below options appear. X-Axis | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's X-axis. ---|--- Y-Axis | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on 2D window's Y-axis. Local | Can type in Internal Line's angle based on the selected segment. 4. Select the desired option. →The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window with different options appears based on your selection. Option | Description ---|--- | X-Axis/ Y-Axis | Local (Pattern outline) | Local (Internal Line) Angle | Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length | Type in Internal Line's length. Extend | When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Opposite Segment | Not Applicable | Internal Line is created based on the other side of the selected line. Reverse | Not Applicable | The Internal Line is reversed. #### Add from a Segment 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the Pattern outline or Internal Line. →The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Add Perpendicular Internal Line. → The Internal Line preview appears at the center of the selected Pattern outline or Internal Line. → The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. 4. Configure below options as needed and click OK. Option | Description ---|--- Angle | Type in the angle for the Internal Line. As the default angle is 90º, you may easily create Internal Line perpendicularly. Length | Type in the length of the Internal Line. Distance to Segment Edge | Locate the Internal Line. The Internal Line preview shifts as number changes. Extend | When the option is toggled on, the Internal Line extends to Pattern outlines. When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. Reverse | The Internal Line is reversed. → The Internal Line is created accordingly.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for adding perpendicular internal lines to 2D patterns using the editing tools in the software.

title: Set View Control (Above ver. 8)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software menu according to user preference in User Settings. Upon restarting, the user settings of the software become the default settings. Shortcut keys, menus, graphic options, view controls, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ View Controls Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ View Controls (ver 11) ### Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: ※ Note: A key and mouse control combination can be set for one function. If a combination is repeated, the interface may not work properly. Preset | Select one of the default presets. ---|--- Pan | Select a key and mouse combination for moving the screen. Zoom | Select a key and mouse combination for zooming in or out the screen. Rotate(3D Window) | Select a key and mouse combination for rotating the screen. Popup Menu | Select a key and mouse combination for opening the pop-up menu of the 3D Window. Others | Axis Constraint Key | Select the key that is used to move items across a constrained horizontal axis, vertical axis, or 45º angle. Smart Panning | Toggle on/off the option to Pan automatically based on the location of the mouse cursor while using certain functions. (Ver .2.5.0) Auto Focus (ver5.0.0) | Toggle on to automatically change the 3D window's focus point based on the user's click. Switch back focus to the default when unselected: The 3D window's focus point returns to all objects when an object is not selected. This option only appears when the **Auto Focus** is toggled ON. **View Point** | Default Y-Axis Position | Set the default position of the Y-Axis. Default X-Axis Position | Set the default position of the X-Axis. Default Camera Distance for Viewpoint Shortcuts | Set the distance between the object and the camera when using the shortcut for view control. Change this setting when the default distance is too far away from the small object. (ver4.2.0) ※ Note: Right-Clicks on a MAC By default, right-clicks are disabled on Macs (Magic Mice, as well as others.) However, the right-click gives you access to important pop-up menus in program. You can easily enable right-clicks for your Mac mouse by following the instructions below: 1. Navigate to System Preferences (either from your dock or from the Apple menu on the top left hand corner of the screen.) 2. Select Mouse. 3. The Secondary Click (Click on right side) option will be unchecked. Check it to enable right-clicks. ### Tablet Pen Setting **Pen Button Settings** Tablet Pen pressure available (ver. 10) **2-Button Pen Settings** Set Tablet Pen as the guide below and preset as XP-PEN or WACOM PEN. * Upper Button: Middle Click * Bottom Button: Right Click Move | Hold down the upper button while hovering, move the pen on the tablet. ---|--- Zoom | Hold down the upper button while while the pen tip is touching device, move the pen in the vertical direction. Rotate | Hold down the bottom button while the pen tip is touching or being placed close to the device, move the pen to rotate. * For XP-Pen, the view rotates only when the pen is close to the surface of the tablet. **3-Button Pen Settings** Set Tablet Pen as the guide below and preset as WACOM PEN. * Upper Button: Space Bar Key * Middle Button: Middle Click * Bottom Button: Right Click Simulation | Turn the simulation on or off by pressing the upper button. ---|--- Move | Hold down the middle button while hovering, move the pen on the tablet. Zoom | Hold down the middle button while the pen tip is touching device, move the pen in the vertical direction. Rotate | Hold down the bottom button while the pen tip is touching or being placed close to the device, move the pen to rotate. * For XP-Pen, the view rotates only when the pen is close to the surface of the tablet.
content_description: Customize your software experience by adjusting default settings and control options in User Settings for optimal functionality and ease of use.

title: Project File (*.Zprj) Add
content: ### Objective Add Garments and Avatars contained within Project files to the workspace (ver2.3.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Project ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Project 2. Navigate and select the Project file to be added and click Open. → The Add Project window appears. 3. Apply any detailed settings, then click on the OK button. ※ Note: * #### Add Project Options Object | Garment (.zpac) | Checking the box will add the Garment compressed in the Project file. ---|---|--- Avatar (.avt) | Checking the box will add the Avatar compresses in the Project file. Translation | X | Move added items horizontally along the center of the 3D environment. Y | Move added items vertically along the center of the 3D environment. Z | Move added items front and back along the center of the 3D environment. Unit | Select the measurement unit for translation. * Right click on Project files directly in the [Library window](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000527827-Library%EC%B0%BD) and select Add to Workspace from the pop-up menu to add Garments and/or Avatars contained within Project files.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding Garments and Avatars from Project files to your workspace in version 2.3.0.

title: OBJ Sequence Export
content: ### Objective Export an OBJ Sequence as an OBJ file on every frame of an animation. Exporting a 1 second animation with a 30 fps standard will result in 30 OBJ files being exported. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation ▶ OBJ Sequence ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation ▶ OBJ Sequence → The Save File window opens. 2. Select the desired file and click OK. → The Export OBJ Animation window opens. 3. Set below options as needed and click OK. #### Export OBJ Animation Option Object | Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all patterns. You can select specific patterns by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ※ When utilizing the OBJ (Selected) menu, patterns selected in the 3D and 2D windows are automatically selected and checkbox-ed. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. You can select specific objects by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Select All Graphics and Trims: Select/Deselect all Graphics and Trims. You can select specific Graphics or Trims by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ---|--- Single Object :Exports the selected object as a single object. If you set the sub-object name, the name of the mesh will be the same with the sub-object name when it is saved. (ver. 5.1.4) You can set it to be saved 'Same as file name' or you can specify 'Object Name'. (ver. 5.1.4) | Multiple Objects :Exports the selected object as multiple objects. UnWeld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). | Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Include Internal Shape: Include internal line and/or shape information in export (ver2.3.0). Scale | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation | Entire Area: saves all of the recorded garment animation. Play Area Only: saves only the play area garment animation. Input Frame: Designate and save the frame section. (ver. 5.1.4) You can save the Bone Information for the frame by setting Save with Bone Information (JSON).
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for exporting an OBJ sequence from an animation, detailing the steps and options available for generating multiple OBJ files based on frame settings.

title: Marvelous Designer 12 Retopology Improvements
content: ### Objective Improve the flexibility and ease of use of the Topology Tools within Marvelous Designer. * * * ## Create Topology: ### Location 3D/2D Window Tool Bar ▶ Topology Tools ### New Operation (from Ver.12) ### Cut Topology Faces **→** Existing blue topology faces can be split by drawing new Topology Points/Edges across them. **→** If cut faces result in Ngons, any blue topology faces with more than 4 sides will be highlighted in orange. ### User-Drawn Topology snaps to Internal Lines **→** When the user creates topology, new points can be snapped to Internal Lines/Shapes as well as external pattern boundaries. * * * ## Edit Topology: ### Location 3D/2D Windows Tool Bar ▶ Edit Topology Tool ### New Operation (from Ver.12) ### Display Ghost Topology across Sewing Relationships for Internal Lines **→** When Topology Points meet Internal Lines with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing relationship. ### Drag Select Topology Points **→** Click outside of an area of blue topology and drag across it to select multiple Topology Points at once. **→** Click and hold the 'Shift' Key, then click and drag over an additional area of blue topology to add Topology Points to an existing selection. ### Drag Deselect Topology Points **→** Click and hold the 'Control' Key, then click and drag over an existing selection of Topology Points to remove Topology Points from that selection. * * * ## Patch Topology: ### Location 2D Window Tool Bar ▶ Patch Topology Tool ### New Operation (from Ver.12) ### Snap Patch Topology to Internal Shapes/Lines **→** Patch Topology edges will snap to both external and internal pattern lines and curve points. ### Snap Patch Topology to Convex Curves **→** Patch Topology edges will now snap to both concave and convex curves. **→** If the curvature of an edge is too extreme for a patch to be created, add one or several curve points along the curved edge with the 'Add Point/Split Line' tool to divide the curve into sections with less extreme curvature. ### Evaluate Patch Validity at Creation **→** After closing a Topology Patch and clicking 'Create', if the drawn patch would create overlapping geometry, an error window pop-up will be raised - return to the Patch Topology tool and update the patch as necessary to avoid overlapping edges/vertices. **→** If the drawn patch would not result in overlapping geometry, the Topology Patch will be created and displayed in blue.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to enhance user experience by detailing new features and improvements in the Topology Tools of Marvelous Designer, enabling users to create, edit, and patch topology with greater flexibility and efficiency.

title: Adjust Avatar Location
content: ### Objective Adjust avatar location by using its X-Ray joint points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X) 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X) 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show X-Ray Joints (Shift + X) 2. Select purple point (pelvis point) in the middle of the avatar. 3. Click and drag or move it with the Gizmo to relocate the avatar.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting an avatar's position using its X-Ray joint points in a 3D environment.
